posts.title: William Hampton, the last hanging in Cornwall.
posts.description: July 20, 1909 dawned wet, grey, cold and gloomy. Unseasonably so, but entirely appropriate for the grim task at hand. The gallows at Bodmin Gaol was already prepared, set to deliver a precisely-calculated drop to the man sat in one of the three ‘Condemned Cells’ only fifty feet from the pit and its waiting noose. It would be the last walk former miner William Hampton would ever make. He didn’t seem too bothered about making it, either. Hampton would be the last Cornishman to hang in the county. After him Cornwall’s condemned would hang at Devon’s Exeter Prison and finally at Bristol. Never again would Bodmin Gaol toll its bell or hoist a black flag to signify the sentence had been carried out. Like Bodmin’s new gallows, used only once before Hampton, the ‘Condemned Cells’ lay unused and eventually forgotten thereafter.
